lit.'<p>Al soltar la esfera, la energía pote:
'

When the ball is released, potential energy turns into kinetic energy: Ek = ½·m·v². At the bottom, all the initial Ep has become Ek: m·g·h = ½·m·v² → v = √(2·g·h), which does not depend on mass. From 5 m it reaches 9.9 m/s.

'
lit.'<p>Con <b>roce</b>, la energía mecánica:
'

With friction, mechanical energy decreases: part of it is dissipated as thermal energy (red bar). The ball no longer reaches the initial height and ends at rest at the bottom. Total energy (mechanical + thermal) is still conserved: initial Em = final Em + Q.

'
lit.'<p>La <b>energía potencial gravitatoria:
'

Gravitational potential energy is the energy linked to height: Ep = m·g·h. A 2 kg ball 5 m above the bottom of the track has 98 J. Twice the height, twice the energy. Height is measured from a reference level we choose (here, the bottom of the track).

'
lit.'<p>La <b>potencia</b> mide qué tan rápi:
'

Power measures how fast energy is transferred: P = W/t, in watts (W = J/s). Lifting the same crate 5 m (980 J) in 10 s takes 98 W; doing it in 5 s, 196 W. The work is the same, but a more powerful motor does it in less time.

'
lit.'<p>Sin roce, la <b>energía mecánica</b>:
'

Without friction, mechanical energy Em = Ep + Ek is conserved: the Ep and Ek bars rise and fall, but their sum does not change. That is why the ball returns to the same height on the other side and oscillates forever. It is a very useful principle: it gives speeds without knowing the details of the path.

'
lit.'<p>Una fuerza realiza <b>trabajo</b> cu:
'

A force does work when it moves the body along its direction: W = F·d·cos θ, in joules (J). The crane lifts a 20 kg crate at constant speed: the force equals the weight (196 N) and lifting it 5 m does W = 196 · 5 = 980 J. That work is stored as potential energy.

'
